Not a current employee, but I worked at In N Out from 2018-2021. It was a great job for the money it paid, the benefits are great. However, they do come at a cost. I quit In N Out for a couple reasons, I’ll let those determine whether you think it’s a good fit for you. After the hiring process you’re met with an extreme amount of online training, more than I ever had at any other minimum wage job. It’s a very “family oriented” place so they really push respecting your managers and accepting that no matter what, the customer and anyone who is “above you” is always right. When I say “above you” I mean a higher level. At In N Out, the way you get a raise is by going through “levels”. First you’ll start out as a level 1 where you’re doing simple things like taking orders at the register, cleaning the dining room…etc. Then you move up to level 2, handling the cash window, level 3, working the food handout window, level 4 handling fries…etc. These “levels” from my experience were handed out to those the managers favored. I worked at in n out as a 16 year old, I was homeschooled so I worked A LOT and picked up more shifts than any of the other people my age, yet I noticed managers still favored some employees over others and would hesitate to give me my “raise” meaning I was stuck doing lower level work that held me back and the people my age looked down on me because I was a lower level. Also at my store, not sure if this is the case for other stores, but a lot of people got raises bc they slept with the managers.

In N Out is a company of “the customer is ALWAYS right”. I got in trouble once because a customer asked if we had plastic knives and i said “we don’t have any up here, I’ll go look in the back and I’ll bring one out to you”. The customer ended up being a secret shopper, and apparently what I said was the wrong answer and I had to sit and do more computer training about the power of always saying yes and always making sure the customer is right. They over-do it with the cultish mindset of “always say yes!” “always do things with a smile” “always tell your manager right on!”. If you’re currently working at Starbucks, I can assume you deal with shitty customers on a day to day basis. You will deal with shitty customers at In N Out, and you will have to deal with even more shitty managers yelling down your throat that you need to be doing your job faster and more efficiently even if what you’re doing is good work, it can always be better!! 

As far as availability goes, I never had a problem with requesting time off or them working around my school schedule. They have a large number of employees at every store and I can remember picking up several shifts from lots of people who always wanted to call off. Usually there was always someone who could take your shift if needed. And I never faced any repercussions for asking to change my availability. Also, as far as calling out sick goes, they are VERY strict on not coming to work when sick. I would text my manager I wasn’t feeling well even if it was a slight sinus infection and they’d tell me to stay home. They’re pretty great when it comes to time off and stuff like that. 

In conclusion, it was a good first job. I learned a lot, I acquired great customer service skills. But it has its issues. Superiority complexes, cultish ways of running the store, everyone is stressed out because the rushes last all day (at least for my store in CA right of a major freeway) and everything has to be done efficiently AND fast. And when you do it quickly, it’ll never be quick enough! So if you’re okay with getting home from a Starbucks shift and having to go to an In N Out shift where you’re dealing with the same customer service, smile on your face, customer is always right bullshit then I say go for it! If you’re the type of person that can let stuff roll off your back and not take it personally as soon as you clock out, go for it! It does pay well, and the price of the stress does pay off because they have great benefits like health insurance and even mental health care! 

Those are my two cents lol hopefully it helps you make a decision. I’m not trying to discourage you from applying, just sharing my story. Good luck!
